trust_decision.summary: createURL trusts every route parameter value as already-safe URL path text: it interpolates the value straight into the URI at the wildcard push (src/client/helpers.ts:133) and at the named/optional-param push (src/client/helpers.ts:150-151), so a value like '/evil.example.com' becomes a protocol-relative Location header once Redirect.toRoute writes the built URL out.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is about open redirects, so an engineer looks first at Redirect.toRoute, which forwards caller params to the router's urlFor and then writes the result into the Location header; that wrapper is a thin pass-through, not the place where the URL is assembled.

fix_sites.entry_point: router.urlBuilder.urlFor (src/client/url_builder.ts:74) and Redirect.toRoute (src/redirect.ts:314), reached through the wildcard branch of createURL
fix_sites.module_kind: public URL-builder helper in the 'client' subpath module (src/client/helpers.ts), imported by the server helpers at src/helpers.ts:20

fix_sites.entry_point: urlFor.get/post/put/patch/delete/method (src/client/url_builder.ts:78-176), router.makeUrl (src/router/main.ts:746), router.makeSignedUrl (src/router/main.ts:773), router.builderForDomain().make() (src/router/legacy/url_builder.ts:123), signedUrlFor (src/router/signed_url_builder.ts:72) - all through the named/optional-param branch of createURL
fix_sites.module_kind: same shared helper module; the fix is one function with two branches

O3_reason_to_dismiss: createSignedURL (src/helpers.ts:194-206) and the deprecated makeUrl/makeSignedUrl (src/router/main.ts:741-745, 767-772) and the legacy UrlBuilder are a separate, lower-level, '@deprecated' URL-making surface, so a solver can argue the redirect bug belongs only to Redirect.toRoute and leave those callers alone - they are covered only because they all funnel into createURL.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Wildcard params are joined with '/' to produce several real path segments - the existing test urlFor('users.list', { '*': ['1','2','3'] }) === '/users/1/2/3' and the prefixUrl/qs options ('https://adonisjs.com/users', '?page=1&sort=name') must stay unencoded, so an over-broad fix that encodes the joined segment string or the final URI breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: required named param as a string (token type 1)
optional param (token type 3), same interpolation branch as required params
wildcard param as string[] supplied under the '*' key, encoded element-by-element then joined with '/'
wildcard param supplied positionally as a params tuple slice
non-string values coerced with String(value) (e.g. numeric id)
values containing '/', '\\', '?' and '#' inside a single segment
params passed as an object map versus a positional array

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the disableRouteLookup branch of makeUrl builds a URL straight from parseRoute(identifier) and the caller's params, bypassing the route store
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already duplicates the URL-construction branch of makeUrl, so a maintainer adding a pattern-based builder would copy the same interpolation next to it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: createSignedURL builds the URL twice - once for the signature (src/helpers.ts:195) and once for the final URL (src/helpers.ts:203) - so any second encoding site must hold for both
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding signing purposes or extra query handling would touch these two createURL calls without re-checking param encoding.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: toPath accepts an already-built URL string and only runs it through encodeUrl, with no param handling of its own
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding a toUrl()/toRoute() variant that takes params (e.g. for referrer or back redirects) would extend this method rather than createURL.

O9_family: CWE-601 open redirect via missing output encoding of route parameters in generated URLs

O10_build.toolchain: npm; tsdown + tsc for build, japa runner via 'node --import=@poppinss/ts-exec --enable-source-maps bin/test.ts' (package.json:36), eslint as pretest
